summary.intent: Determine why native git outperforms gix for Callisto's history walk, whether Callisto could use gix optimally, and which upstream gix performance contributions are worth pursuing; then hand the work off to a new session.
summary.outcome: Analysis located the gap in wide-tree pack delta decoding and cache behavior (not diff resource cache), ranked contribution candidates, cloned gitoxide to ~/projects/gix with a handoff note at etc/plan/callisto-history-performance.md, and produced a detailed goal-and-outcome prompt for the next session. No Callisto code changed and the reported timings were not independently reproduced.

repo: Callisto uses system git only per ADR 0005 (docs/adr/0005-system-git-only.md); reintroducing gix requires a superseding ADR (proposed ADR 13) that the user must accept per AGENTS.md.
The old gix backend lived in crates/callisto-vcs (removed in commit 7ad333311); current Git access is crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs, with the changed-paths history command near line 510.
Callisto's hot path collects changed paths for the whole history window then maps them to packages; it is not a path-filtered git log, so Bloom filters do not help it.

Reported benchmarks (4000 pkgs/8002 commits): history walk git ~730-1020ms vs gix ~3.3-3.6s; manifest reads gix ~200ms vs git ~255ms; tag listing roughly equal. At 500 pkgs gix is 3.5x faster, crossover near 2000.
Callisto-side costs found separately were its own algorithms (quadratic aggregation ~640ms, tag glob matching ~220ms), not gix defects.
Correctness rule for Callisto: a commit counts if reachable from HEAD xor tag (symmetric); any gix comparison must reproduce that, including merges and hotfix branches.
Gitoxide already tracks pack delta caching and Bloom filters in etc/plan/performance.md; it asks for a discussion before changes above ~500 source lines.

code.finding: Cached decoder appears to cache only the final requested object, whereas git's unpack_entry caches intermediate delta bases; a candidate cause of repeated inflation.
Outcome describes total decompressed chain bytes but the delta path assigns the requested entry's decompressed size, so the statistic is inaccurate for instrumentation.
Default pack cache is a fixed 64-entry LRU; configuring core.deltaBaseCacheLimit switches to a memory-capped hashmap, so the 1GB result conflates cache size and policy.
Fixed cache can clear all entries when its memory limit is exceeded.
High-level revision walk Info omits the root tree ID that gix-commitgraph already exposes (file/commit.rs:93); obtaining it currently reads the commit object.
for_each_to_obtain_tree creates a diff resource cache per call; _with_cache variant reuses it, but measured gain was small (3.3s to 3.0s).

workflow: Handoff prompts for long-running goal runs need explicit stages, completion criteria, and a stated skepticism of unverified numbers; the user pushed back that the first prompt was too light.
Benchmark fairness requires identical output, same pack, and separating cache size from cache policy; noisy machine (concurrent compile) gives ~±15% error.
Research relied on reading vendored crate sources in ~/.cargo/registry plus WebSearch; the original spike source was unavailable in the workspace.

friction: The original gix spike source and fixture were not available, so causal claims could not be verified and some earlier analysis had to be corrected mid-session (e.g., Bloom filters, per-call cache).
Benchmarks were noisy because another process was compiling on the machine.
Duplicate user message and initial handoff prompt lacking detail required a rewrite.
Case mismatch between ~/projects and ~/Projects directories required checking.
open_items: Build a reproducible wide-tree fixture and benchmark (500/2000/4000 flat plus sharded control) comparing git and gix on the same pack.
Test the intermediate-delta-base caching hypothesis and compare no/fixed/dynamic caches at equal budgets (96MiB, 256MiB, 1GiB).
Possible small gix PR: expose root tree ID in revision walk Info; fix decoder Outcome statistics.
Bloom filter reader and path-limited history in gix as a separate longer-term contribution.
Prototype an exact commit-to-changed-paths index at the application level.
Callisto decisions pending: opt-in gix read backend pilot, ADR 13 superseding ADR 5, backend selection policy, merge handling via per-parent diff intersection tested against --cc.
Handoff note in ~/projects/gix is uncommitted; no upstream issue or PR should be posted without user authorization.
